messages.author: 10f08b7c54c082e7
messages.subject: Mixture distributions for priors?
parts:
I am using Stan to estimate parameters of a covariance function, similar to that given on page 87 of the Stan Users' Guide. This has been very useful for analyzing my data at a fixed point in time.

I would now like to extend it to a simple time-varying case. I expect the covariance function parameters estimated at time t to be similar to those at time t+1, so it would be nice if I could use the posterior distribution for the parameters at time t as a prior for the parameters at time t+1. In general, standard prior distributions that I have used in Stan would not fit the observed parameter posterior distributions well. Instead, I would like to find a kernel density estimate of the posterior distribution at time t (outside Stan), and code it in Stan at time t+1 using a mixture distribution prior. Can mixture distributions be used as priors in Stan? If not, I'd be very interested in other ways of approaching this problem.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixture distributions for priors? [time series of covariance matrices]
parts:
Yes, you can use mixtures in Stan. There's a chapter
in the modeling language manual on discrete mixtures and we
discuss some continuous mixture parameterizations in the reparameterization
chapter.

I didn't understand what you meant going on outside Stan. As
long as it's done ahead of time and passed in as data you can
use it.

You might also try fitting it as a time series, but I don't know
what kind of distributions would be useful there --- Ben and Andrew
probably have advice here.

That would work out to be a stochastic volatility model, but with
covariance matrices, not just variances in the time series.

- Bob
